newsitem.title: USA: G7 agrees on debt relief, aid to start soon - Clarke.
newsitem.headline: G7 agrees on debt relief, aid to start soon - Clarke.

text.p: The Group of Seven Finance Ministers have reached agreement on the need to help the world's poorest debtor nations, UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Saturday.
"I hope we will be able to have the first countries to benefit from (the debt initiative)...before the end of the year," he told reporters after the G7 meeting here.
"We can all be satisfied that finance will be forthcoming...one way or the other," Clarke said.
Clarke did not say whether the discussions touched on methods of financing other than controversial gold sales.

Britain, the U.S. and some other countries have urged the International Monetary Fund sell some of its gold to cover the gap in funding requrements until a permanent and self-financing enhanced structural adjustment facility for the world's poorest indebted countries can be be put in place.
Germany and Italy have been opposed to gold sales.
Clarke said that there would be agreement at Sunday's IMF Interim Committee meeting on proposals to increase Paris Club debt forgiveness to a maximum of 80 percent from the current 67 percent.
He also expected early conclusion on proposals for a new agreement to borrow to bolster the IMF's ability to help member countries in an emergency.
